title: Gradient boosting & XGBoost
summary: Add trees that correct the current ensemble using local gradients and curvature.
why: Fits nonlinear tabular relationships through sequential residual correction.
interview: Derive optimal leaf weights and regularized split gain.
derivation: For a fixed leaf assignment, group gradients and Hessians into G_j and H_j. Differentiate G_j*w_j + 0.5*(H_j+lambda)*w_j^2; setting the derivative to zero yields the optimal weight.

Functional gradient descent adds a function in the direction that reduces loss. XGBoost uses a second-order approximation plus explicit tree complexity penalties; histogram search, sparsity handling, and column subsampling improve engineering efficiency.

explanations.title: Boosting adds a correction function
paragraphs: An additive ensemble predicts F_t(x)=F_(t-1)(x)+eta*f_t(x). Gradient boosting fits the next function to a direction that reduces loss with respect to current predictions. For squared error this direction is the residual; for other losses it is the negative gradient.

XGBoost approximates the incremental objective using first derivatives g_i and second derivatives h_i of the loss at current predictions. Tree complexity penalties regularize the number of leaves and leaf weights.

Trees are trained sequentially because each stage depends on the current ensemble. Parallel split evaluation and data processing inside a stage do not make the boosting dependence disappear. Smaller learning rates usually require more trees and validation-based stopping.

explanations.title: Derive leaf weights and split gain
paragraphs: For a fixed tree structure, sum gradients G_j and Hessians H_j inside each leaf. The leaf objective is G_j*w_j + 0.5*(H_j+lambda)*w_j^2 plus the per-leaf complexity cost. Setting the derivative to zero gives w_j=-G_j/(H_j+lambda).

Substituting optimal weights gives the score improvement from a split. The child score sum must exceed the parent score plus gamma, the extra-leaf penalty. This derivation assumes the stated L2 regularizer; L1 regularization changes the weight formula.
For GL=4,HL=2,GR=-2,HR=2,lambda=1,gamma=0, the gain is 0.5*(16/3+4/3-4/5), approximately 2.933. Child weights are -1.333 and 0.667. Apply eta when adding their predictions to the ensemble.

explanations.title: Split search, missing values, and validation
paragraphs: Histogram methods bin feature values and aggregate gradient statistics rather than testing every raw threshold. Sparsity-aware handling can learn a default branch for missing values. A missing entry and a measured zero are not automatically equivalent.

Control overfitting using tree depth or leaf limits, row and column subsampling, regularization, learning rate, and early stopping on a valid split. Do not select the number of rounds on the final test set.

For temporal prediction, training rows and features must respect event time. A boosted tree can exploit future-derived aggregates as efficiently as any other model. Compare ranking, probability calibration, and business thresholds under the deployment distribution.
